entries.what_happened: Fourteen manuscripts. The ones that bear on the bullet: (1) 'Log abundance in characteristic zero' (Sept 24) claims log abundance for normal projective lc pairs (X,B) over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero: B effective rational, K+B Q-Cartier and nef, then some positive Cartier multiple of K+B is globally generated. The B=0 klt case is the bullet. The proof is a dimension induction over C, with descent to other algebraically closed fields. It also claims canonical nonvanishing for smooth projective varieties over C in every dimension, and good log minimal models for pseudo-effective projective lc adjoints. (2) 'Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity' (Oct 6) claims, over C and conditionally on a stated subadditivity assumption, that an analytically nef K+Δ on a normal irreducible compact Kähler lc pair with effective rational Δ and Q-Cartier K+Δ is semiample, in every dimension. Projective varieties are compact Kähler, so Δ=0 gives the bullet over C, conditionally. (3) 'Conditional good minimal models for compact Kähler fourfolds' (Oct 6) has, in its projective appendix, conditional projective log abundance: normal projective lc over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field with nef Q-Cartier K+B is semiample, given logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity. Its main theorem is conditional good minimal models for klt compact Kähler fourfolds. (4) 'Abundance after nonvanishing for compact Kähler fourfolds' (Sept 27) claims that for a normal connected compact Kähler klt fourfold with effective rational Δ and analytically nef Q-Cartier K+Δ, K+Δ is semiample once κ(X,K+Δ)≥0 (nonvanishing is a hypothesis). If κ=0 the adjoint is trivial. Projectivity and Q-factoriality are not assumed. (5) 'Lifting sections from the reduced support of an adjoint' (Sept 27) claims: a supported-boundary lifting theorem for projective Q-factorial dlt pairs (positive Iitaka dimension when a Cartier multiple supported on the reduced boundary restricts to a semiample bundle on that whole boundary); abundance after nonvanishing for projective lc pairs of dimension at most 4 over C; a fourfold log abundance corollary for lc pairs of dimension at most 4 over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, which takes its nonvanishing from (6); and a conditional reduction in all dimensions, assuming smooth canonical nonvanishing in every dimension. (6) 'Fourfold nonvanishing by minimal metrics and moving jets' (Sept 27) claims canonical nonvanishing for smooth connected projective complex fourfolds (K pseudo-effective implies H^0(mK) nonzero for some m). Its Corollary 1.2 gives nonvanishing for projective lc pairs of dimension at most 4 with effective rational Δ and nef Q-Cartier K+Δ. (7) 'Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints' (Sept 27) claims zero-Lelong minimal semipositive metrics on pullbacks of nef Q-Cartier adjoints of projective klt pairs, and an H^1 injectivity theorem on smooth projective varieties. It is an analytic input, not an abundance statement. (8) 'Uniform indices for semi-log-canonical log Calabi-Yau pairs' (Oct 5) claims, for each dimension d≥4 and finite coefficient set Φ, a uniform integer a(d,Φ) such that a(K+B) is Cartier and trivial for every connected projective slc log Calabi-Yau pair (K+B ~Q 0) with coefficients in Φ. With B=0 and X klt this covers klt varieties with K_X ~Q 0. (9) 'Uniform Pluricanonical Iitaka Fibrations' (Oct 3) claims a uniform pluricanonical degree m(d) whose complete system defines the Iitaka fibration of every smooth projective d-fold with κ≥0 (Theorem 1.1), and a uniform index a(d,Φ) for projective lc pairs with K+B ~Q 0 (Theorem 1.2). Both use the log-abundance paper. (10) 'Uniform log Iitaka fibrations and bounded moduli denominators' (Oct 4) claims, for d≥5 and finite coefficients, a uniform degree at which the complete rounded system of an lc pair with κ≥0 generates the full Iitaka field. (11) 'Uniform effective log Iitaka fibrations for fourfolds' (Sept 26) claims the four-dimensional finite-coefficient effective log Iitaka statement, and a uniform canonical index N_4 with N_4 K_X ~ 0 for normal projective klt fourfolds with K_X ~Q 0. (12) 'Relative denominators and effective systems for log Calabi-Yau fibrations' (Sept 27) gives denominator and effective-system bounds for log Calabi-Yau fibrations from lc pairs of dimension at most 4. (13) 'Arithmetic Stein-degree bounds for log Calabi-Yau pairs' (Sept 25) bounds the constant-field degree [k_S:k] of each component S of B with coefficient at least t. (14) 'Schnell fiber spaces and good canonical models' (Sept 24) proves the Campana-Peternell inequality κ(X)≥κ(D), and κ(X)=κ(F)+dim Y for fibre spaces under a pseudo-effectivity hypothesis. Items 12-14 make no semiampleness claim. For 12-14 I read only the abstracts and opening sections.
entries.delivers: For the bullet as worded (normal projective klt variety, nef canonical bundle, conclusion: semiample), the strongest claim is (1). It claims the bullet's case in every dimension over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with K_X Q-Cartier. The paper states this as a positive answer to the characteristic-zero log abundance conjecture. Its statement matches the list's in dimension and in class: klt is lc with Δ=0, nef is the same hypothesis, and semiample is the same conclusion. The bullet names no field, and the live article says over a field k. The claim reaches only algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields. Dimension at most 4 over such fields is also claimed by the fourfold corollary in (5), which takes nonvanishing from (6) and does not rely on the all-dimensional induction. The compact Kähler paper (2), the conditional appendix of (3), and the reduction in (5) give the bullet only under their stated premises. The rationally trivial special case, K_X ~Q 0, is also covered by the index statements (8), (9) and (11). Those give integral triviality of a multiple rather than semiampleness of a general nef class. A nef, numerically trivial K_X that is not Q-linearly trivial falls under (1) only.
entries.remains: If (1) is correct, the bullet is covered for algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero in every dimension. Still open for the bullet: positive characteristic, and characteristic-zero fields that are not algebraically closed. The bullet names none of these, and the family does not claim them. The all-dimensional coverage rests on (1) alone. If (1)'s induction failed, what would remain claimed is dimension at most 4, through (5) and (6), and the compact Kähler and conditional statements under their premises.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture for projective lc pairs in characteristic zero over algebraically closed fields, in all dimensions (claimed); dimension-4 and compact-Kähler versions are conditional or dimension-limited; the index papers prove the rationally trivial case
entries.conditional_on: (1) The zero-boundary logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity is used in the Albanese step (Lemma ex:irregularity). It is cited as Corollary 6.2 of 'Orbifold and logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity', an OpenAI preprint outside this family that I did not read. The text says that same application also follows from Hacon-Popa-Schnell and Cao-Paun. (2) Assumes logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity for smooth projective varieties with reduced SNC boundaries, the same outside result; takes its projective good-model input from (1). (3) The projective appendix assumes logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, reached from an orbifold-subadditivity assumption that the text labels a theorem of the outside 'Orbifold and logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity' preprint. The main theorem also assumes a pseudo-effective fourfold MMP (outside OpenAI preprint 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds') and effective fourfold abundance, which is (4). (4) Assumes κ≥0 (nonvanishing) as a hypothesis. Positive Iitaka dimension is delegated to Höring-Lazić-Lehn, Theorem 4.1 (external). The threefold floor input is Das-Ou, Corollary 1.3 (external). (5) The fourfold corollary uses (6), Corollary 1.2. The all-dimensional reduction assumes smooth canonical nonvanishing in every dimension (Hashizume's Conjecture 1.3). (6) Uses the moving-center lemmas 7.1-7.5 and Theorem 9.1 of (1), the analytic inputs of (7), and Hashizume's Theorem 1.4 for the lc extension. (8), (9), (10), (11) use the good-model theorem of (1) (Theorem 11.1 as cited); (8) also uses the normal index theorem of (9), external results of Birkar (2025), and Jiang-Liu for dimension at most 3. (10) also uses (13).
entries.doubts: (a) Abstract versus dependencies: the Uniform Pluricanonical abstract says 'We prove the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture in characteristic zero' and does not mention that the proof uses (1); the introduction says it does. The Uniform indices abstract says the paper 'resolves' the slc index conjecture and does not mention its reliance on the good-model theorem of (1). (b) The projective good-model section of the compact Kähler paper (03b) is a compressed argument that cites numbered theorems and lemmas of Fujino's analytic MMP paper (Theorem E, Theorem 8.3, Lemmas 11.13-11.17). I did not check those citations. (c) In the abundance-after-nonvanishing paper, the positive-Iitaka branch is delegated to Höring-Lazić-Lehn, and the finiteness argument for non-projective surface strata (returning chains, a groupoid that 'may have infinitely many arrows') is one paragraph. The paper calls the surface mechanism prior art. (d) The log-abundance paper's introduction says of the compatibility step: 'The proof must still identify the obstruction to lifting and show that these ordinary-variety results apply to the covering construction.' I did not check the sections where that argument is carried out. (e) The lifting paper's core argument (its supported-boundary theorem) is summarized in a few paragraphs of its introduction. I did not check its sections. (f) The lifting paper's introduction also states, without using it in the theorems, a conormal-period result for smooth fourfolds with nef K and κ=0 (no ν=2). I did not read that section.
